response.title: Harborlight's FY2027 Budget and a Sixth Site

segments.heading: The main ask
segments.text: Staff are asking the board to approve an FY2027 budget of $1,610,000. The money would open a sixth site at the Eastgate branch library. It would also add two site coordinators. Staff estimate the new site would serve 180 more learners a year. They also estimate it would cut the waitlist in half. The board agreed to vote on the FY2027 budget on October 21. Below are the key facts.

segments.heading: Who Harborlight served
segments.text: Let's start with who Harborlight served. In fiscal year 2026, Harborlight enrolled 1,148 adult learners across five neighborhood sites. The year before, it enrolled 936. This year, 412 learners worked toward a high school equivalency credential. And 389 were English language learners. The results were strong. Sixty-eight percent of learners who stayed at least 12 weeks gained one or more reading levels on the CASAS assessment. Seventy-one learners earned a high school equivalency credential. No year in Harborlight's history has seen more.

segments.heading: Tutors, staff and funding
segments.text: Next come people and money. A corps of 214 volunteer tutors gave 9,870 tutoring hours. On average, a tutor stayed 14 months. Harborlight has 11 full-time staff. Four of them are site coordinators. FY2026 operating expenses were $1,420,000. Program costs made up 81 percent of spending. Foundation grants gave $640,000. Individual donors gave $388,000. The city's adult education contract paid $295,000. Each learner cost $1,237.

segments.heading: Adults still waiting
segments.text: Then there is the waitlist. At year end, 287 adults were on it. Most of them were waiting for the Eastgate and Riverside sites. The average wait was nine weeks. Staff say the new Eastgate site would cut that waitlist in half. A learner at the Riverside site summed up what is at stake. The learner said, "I read my granddaughter a bedtime story for the first time this spring."

segments.heading: Reserves and what comes next
segments.text: Last, reserves and next steps. Dev Patel, the treasurer, reported that reserves stand at 3.2 months of operating expenses. The board's target is 4 months, so reserves fall short. The board asked staff to bring a one-page summary of the FY2027 budget request to the October 21 board meeting. Board members also asked for a short deck. They plan to use it with funders when they talk about the sixth site.

response.recap: Keep three things in mind. First, staff want the board to approve an FY2027 budget of $1,610,000, which adds a sixth site at the Eastgate branch library. Second, 287 adults were on the waitlist at year end, and the average wait was nine weeks. Third, reserves stand at 3.2 months of operating expenses, short of the board's target of 4 months.
